title: Potato Dauphinoise
subtitle: Baked sliced potato in cream and garlic
excerpt: Thinly sliced waxy potatoes baked slowly in seasoned cream and garlic until tender and yielding, with a golden, bubbling crust. Rich, indulgent, and deeply satisfying.

recipe.sourceNotes: Gratin dauphinois (or potatoes Dauphinoise in British English) originates in the Dauphiné region of southeastern France, where it was first documented in the late eighteenth century. The dish is deceptively simple: thinly sliced potato, cream, garlic, and salt, baked slowly in the oven until the cream reduces and the potato slices soften and absorb it, while the top forms a golden gratin. Arguments over the correct recipe are longstanding in France: some versions include Gruyère cheese on top; the traditional Dauphiné version has no cheese at all. Adding cheese makes it closer to gratin Savoyard, which uses cheese and stock rather than cream. The key technique is the mandoline or very sharp knife: the slices must be uniformly thin (2 to 3 mm) so they cook at the same rate.

recipeTools.notes: A 20 x 30 cm baking dish, about 5 cm deep.

content.text: Do not rinse the potato slices after cutting: the starch on the cut surface helps to thicken the cream as the dish cooks. Slice on a mandoline or with a very sharp knife to an even 2 to 3 mm thickness. Rub the baking dish generously with a cut garlic clove and butter before layering. Season each layer as you build. The dish is done when a knife slides through the centre with no resistance and the cream has been mostly absorbed and the top is golden.

items.preparation: thinly sliced, about 2 to 3 mm; do not rinse
for the dish and dotting on top

content.text: Heat the oven to 170 C / fan 150 C / gas 3. Rub a deep baking dish with the cut garlic clove and then butter it generously. Warm the cream, milk, crushed garlic, salt, pepper, and nutmeg in a saucepan until just steaming. Do not boil.
Layer the potato slices in the dish, overlapping like scales. Pour the warm cream mixture over the potato, pressing the layers down so they are submerged. Dot the top with butter.
Bake for 70 to 80 minutes until the top is golden and a knife passes through with no resistance. If the top is browning too quickly, cover loosely with foil. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.
